connections.title: Connection Details
connections.name: Connection Name
connections.authAgentIdentityHint: Pin one to present only that key to the server (less fingerprint exposure). Default offers all, like ssh.
connections.authAgentNoneHint: Start one and add a key — eval "$(ssh-agent)" then ssh-add — then reopen this dialog.
connections.authAgentNote: Rite asks the agent to sign — your key and passphrase never leave it, and nothing is stored in Rite. Hardware keys (YubiKey/FIDO) work only this way.
connections.authAgentForwardHint: Lets the remote machine reuse your local keys to hop onward. Powerful but risky — leave off unless you need it.
connections.keyPassphrasePlaceholder: Enter passphrase if key is encrypted...
connections.collectionMoveUnsupported: Moving a machine between collections isn't supported yet.
connections.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this connection?
connections.keyFileHint: Read in this page and stored in your encrypted vault — it is never uploaded as a file. Terminals here run on the server, so a path on your computer would mean nothing to it.
connections.keyFileLoaded: Loaded from {name}. It is encrypted with your vault key before it leaves this page.
connections.keyUnreadable: That file could not be read.
connections.keyLooksPublic: That looks like a public key (.pub). Choose the private key — the file without the extension.
connections.keyRememberWhy: Otherwise it is asked each time you connect. Kept here it rides with the key it protects, so it stops being a second barrier.
connections.keyRememberOff: Your server does not keep passphrases
connections.keyRememberOffWhy: — you will be asked for it each time you connect.
connections.passphraseAskWhy: Used for this connection only. Rite is not keeping it — tick “Remember this passphrase” when editing the machine if you would rather it did.
connections.keyPassphraseStored: A passphrase is stored for this key. Leave this empty to keep it, type a new one to replace it, or untick below to have Rite forget it.
connections.keyRememberForget: Stored. Untick to have Rite forget it — you will be asked for it at each connection instead.
connections.passwordRememberWhy: Otherwise it is asked each time you connect, and Rite writes it nowhere.
connections.passwordRememberForget: Stored. Untick to have Rite forget it — you will be asked at each connection instead.
connections.passwordRememberOff: Your server does not keep passwords
connections.passwordRememberOffWhy: — you will be asked for it each time you connect.
connections.passwordStored: A password is stored. Leave this empty to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
connections.passwordLeaveEmpty: Leave empty to keep the current password.
connections.passwordAskWhy: Used for this connection only. Rite is not keeping it — tick “Remember this password” when editing the machine if you would rather it did.

jump.label: Jump host
jump.hint: Reach this machine through another (a bastion). Rite opens the jump first, then tunnels the SSH session to the target — like OpenSSH ProxyJump. Chainable: if the jump itself has a jump, the whole path is built. Your key never lands on the bastion.

users.subtitle: Accounts on this instance
users.confirmPromote: Promote {name} to admin? They get full server access and can read collection names through the Admin group.
users.awaitingTitle: Provisioned — has not set their own password yet
users.resetWhy: Use this when {name} has lost their password. Verify it is really them first, in person or by phone. Set a temporary password to relay to them; they set their own at next login.

invites.title: Invitations
invites.subtitle: Enrollment tokens · single-use
invites.banner: Redeeming a token grants membership and its role at once. It does not grant a collection's encrypted machines — those still need a member grant, as they always do.
invites.revealWhy: You won't see it again. Share it out-of-band, not by email in clear.
invites.empty: No invitation tokens yet. Generate one to onboard a member without being present.
invites.genWhy: The holder registers themselves, with the role and teams you pick below already applied. The token is single-use and shown once — the server keeps only a hash.
invites.orgRoleAdmin: Admins can mint user or manager tokens (never admin).
invites.orgRoleManager: Managers can mint user tokens only.
invites.neverExpires: The token never expires — revoke it manually.

admin.hiddenNative: Server settings live in the web console — open the server URL in a browser.
admin.hiddenManager: Instance administration is limited to admins.

dash.subtitle: This Rite instance at a glance

admin.zkBody: The server never sees a key. Collection names are readable here only through the Admin-group escrow, and machine credentials stay sealed to members. Collections created before the escrow existed appear by id until re-keyed. You can decrypt names, remove a member, delete a collection, and grant a member access to the name and roster; full machine access still needs a member to seal the item key.

coll.title: Collection governance
coll.subtitle: Policies and oversight, server-wide
coll.allowCreateNote: When off, only admins provision collections.
coll.allowSharingNote: Members can add anyone in the directory, not just teammates.
coll.defaultRoleNote: Applied when someone is added to a collection.
coll.confirmDelete: Force-delete this collection for every member? Its encrypted machines are lost.
coll.grantTitle: Grant access to the name and roster
coll.grantNote: Adds the user to the roster and lets them see the collection name.
coll.grantUnavailable: Available once the collection is escrowed to the Admin group (created after the escrow, or re-keyed).

inst.bindsClient: This binds the client, not the data.
inst.title: Instance
inst.lead: A name for this server, shown on the sign-in screen and in the header.
inst.saved: Saved. It shows after everyone's next reload.
inst.hostKeyShare: Share this so users can pin this server on first connect.
inst.persistence: Keep users signed in across reloads
inst.persistenceDesc: Each vault key sits in that browser's session storage and is cleared when the tab closes; it never leaves the browser. Off: a RAM-only key, so a reload means a re-login.
inst.openRegDesc: On, the sign-in screen offers “Create an account”: anyone who can reach this server registers themselves, as a plain user with no team. Leave off for an invite-only instance.
inst.allowInvDesc: Off closes the enrollment-token path instance-wide: no new tokens, and existing ones stop working. Independent of open registration.
inst.confirmRoleDesc: On, changing a role in Users asks first — a guard against an accidental promotion. A prompt, applied on every client.
inst.capsDesc: What connected clients may do on this server.
inst.shellOpensChoice: What a member gets until they choose otherwise.
inst.shellOpensFixed: Every terminal, for everyone — web-UI members do not pick their own.
inst.shellPrefix: The shell a terminal here opens.
inst.shellDesktop: Desktop users run their own machine's shell. Installed here:
inst.shellChoiceDesc: The default above is then the only shell. On, a member picks among the installed shells in “Settings ▸ Terminals”, and one terminal at a time from the + beside the tabs. They choose a name, never a path.
inst.quickSshDesc: Ad-hoc one-off SSH from the toolbar. Connections on a server belong in collections, saved and auditable. On for teams that need throwaway sessions.
inst.hostKeyModeDesc: One policy for everyone, since every connection runs here. Strict refuses a host key it has not seen; warn and accept do not, so neither would refuse a man-in-the-middle either. Clients show it read-only.
inst.storedSecretsDesc: What may rest in a member's own vault, and whether they can read it back.
inst.secretStorageWhat: An SSH password, a key passphrase, a key carried in the record.
inst.secretStorageDefault: Each member's own box starts unticked. Off: nothing is written and each is asked at every connection.
inst.secretStorageBinds: A record is sealed before it reaches this instance.
inst.secretReveal: Members may read a stored secret back
inst.secretRevealWhen: On an explicit action, and never on screen by itself. Off: the vault is write-only here.
inst.secretRevealBinds: A browser decrypts the record it connects with, so the boundary that holds is who the collection is shared with.
inst.hcDesc: comes from users' own connections and costs nothing.
inst.hcActiveDesc: makes requests from every client — a scan-like footprint at scale — so it is governed here.
inst.showStatusDesc: The passive “last seen” pastille. No probing.
inst.probeLegend: Off is passive only · On-demand probes when a user asks · Full allows background polling · Client's choice lets each client pick its cadence.
inst.methodsDesc: ICMP is blocked on some networks and required on others. Clients may use only a method enabled here.
inst.whoProbesDesc: Empty means everyone. Add usernames to restrict active probing; passive “last seen” stays available to all.
inst.minIntervalDesc: Floor for background polling, so status never saturates the network.
inst.dashDesc: These two cards run a command on the host each time they refresh. The rest of the dashboard reads what Rite already holds.
inst.dashStrength: The two are not equally strong. Web UI is enforcement: this server runs the commands, so off means nothing runs. Clients is policy: a client probes from its own network and this server never sees it — the official client hides the cards, a modified one could ignore the switch.
inst.dashWebuiDesc: This server runs the commands, so its own egress pays. Off is off for everyone in a browser.
inst.dashWebuiLabel: Allow the dashboard probing cards in the web UI
inst.dashClientsDesc: Each client probes from its own network, so your users' endpoints pay. A user may also turn the cards off for themselves; neither side overrides the other upward.
inst.dashClientsLabel: Allow the dashboard probing cards in attached clients
inst.dashIntervalDesc: Floor between automatic refreshes. Clients apply a floor of their own, so a very small number buys little. Pressing Refresh is not limited, and a dashboard nobody watches does not poll.
inst.managedBy: Set by this instance's configuration ({origin}) — change it there, not here.
